![Cover of the Winter/Spring 2026 issue of Dædalus. Image from the [American Academy of Arts & Sciences](https://www.amacad.org/publication/daedalus/unlocking-scientific-intuition-reasoning-at-digital-speed).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="cover-full.jpg"}

[Pushmeet Kohli](https://research.google/people/pushmeet-kohli/), Vice President of Science and Strategic Initiatives at [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/), writes in [Dædalus](https://www.amacad.org/publication/daedalus/unlocking-scientific-intuition-reasoning-at-digital-speed) that AI is the latest instrument in a lineage running from the telescope and microscope: a lens that supplies "machine intuition" for making sense of scientific complexity [[1]](#ref-1). The essay walks through biology, materials science, and mathematics before turning to agentic systems that generate their own hypotheses.

The essay's abstract:

> Throughout history, scientific progress has been defined by the tools we build to extend our perception. Today, artificial intelligence stands as our newest instrument, not merely as a computational engine but as a revolutionary lens for deciphering the nature of reality. Drawing on my research journey at Google DeepMind, this essay explores how scientists are deploying AI to overcome the hardest "root node" bottlenecks in science. By applying machine intuition, we are uncovering breakthroughs across biology, materials science, and mathematics, from solving the grand challenge of protein folding with [AlphaFold](https://deepmind.google/science/alphafold/) to charting new universes of stable materials with [GNoME](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/millions-of-new-materials-discovered-with-deep-learning/). The essay concludes by reflecting on the transition toward open-ended, agentic AI systems that actively generate novel hypotheses and their implications for the nature of scientific inquiry. We are evolving from the solvers of intricate puzzles into the architects of profound questions, embarking on the most exciting journey of discovery ever undertaken.

The essay is a first-person tour of DeepMind's AI-for-science program, structured as deep dives into three fields. What it covers:

- **The thesis**: AI extends the telescope-microscope-computer lineage by supplying "machine intuition," a learned strategy for finding structure in data too vast for human perception. It targets two limits on inquiry, the scale of what we try to understand and the speed at which we can test ideas, and selects "root node" problems: foundational bottlenecks that experts agree won't fall to existing methods within a decade.
- **Biology**: [AlphaFold 2](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphafold-a-solution-to-a-50-year-old-grand-challenge-in-biology/) solved the fifty-year grand challenge of protein folding to atomic accuracy in 2020 [[2]](#ref-2), and the AlphaFold database now holds structures for more than 200 million proteins used by three million researchers across 190 countries [[3]](#ref-3). AlphaFold 3 extended this to how proteins bind DNA, RNA, and other molecules [[4]](#ref-4), while AlphaMissense classifies DNA variants as benign or harmful [[5]](#ref-5). The essay also credits outside work: EVEscape for forward-looking vaccine design [[6]](#ref-6), David Baker's from-scratch protein design (a shared 2024 Nobel in Chemistry) [[7]](#ref-7), the AI-found antibiotic halicin [[8]](#ref-8), and a petabyte-scale map of a human brain circuit [[9]](#ref-9).
- **Materials science**: GNoME learned to approximate the rules of quantum chemistry and returned 2.2 million candidate materials, 380,000 of them predicted stable, which the essay puts at roughly eight hundred years of progress in a single day [[10]](#ref-10). The candidates still have to be synthesized and tested, where self-driving labs are beginning to help. Related projects include real-time control of fusion-reactor plasma with EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) [[11]](#ref-11) and pulling rare signals from Large Hadron Collider data [[12]](#ref-12).
- **Mathematics**: [AlphaProof](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/ai-solves-imo-problems-at-silver-medal-level/) proves statements in the formal language [Lean](https://lean-lang.org/), where a result is machine-checkable, and with AlphaGeometry it reached silver-medal level at the 2024 [International Mathematical Olympiad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Mathematical_Olympiad). Gemini Deep Think reached gold in 2025 [[13]](#ref-13). The essay is candid that Olympiad problems are not research, and points to [AlphaEvolve](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphaevolve-a-gemini-powered-coding-agent-for-designing-advanced-algorithms/), tested on more than fifty open math problems, where it matched the best known solution in three-quarters of cases and improved on it in a fifth [[14]](#ref-14), as the closer analog to discovery.
- **The forward look**: the essay closes on agentic systems that generate their own hypotheses, a shift from "solvers of intricate puzzles" to "architects of profound questions."
